introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.body:
Blip Toast is a toast library for React Native. It gives you five variants, toasts that follow a promise from loading to done, and a card you can restyle piece by piece or replace entirely.

It has two moving parts. `toastManager` holds the list of live toasts outside React, so `toast()` works from anywhere — a screen, a hook, an API client. `<ToastContainer />`, mounted once, subscribes to that list and owns everything visual: stacking, entrance and exit motion, auto-dismiss and accessibility roles.

There is no provider to wrap your app in and no hook to call before you can show a toast.

installation.title: Installation
installation.body: Install the package together with `react-native-svg`, which draws the built-in icons.
installation.after:
In Expo projects, use `npx expo install blip-toast react-native-svg` so you get the `react-native-svg` version that matches your SDK.

**Requirements:** `react` 18 or later, `react-native` 0.72 or later and `react-native-svg` 13 or later. Reanimated and Gesture Handler are not needed — animations run on React Native's `Animated` API with the native driver.

quick-start.title: Quick start
quick-start.body: Mount `<ToastContainer />` once, as the last child of your root component, so it renders above everything else.

variants.title: Variants
variants.body: Five variants, each with its own icon and accent colour. Plain `toast()` uses `default`.
variants.after: There is a sixth phase, `loading`, drawn with a spinner. You rarely set it by hand: `toast.promise()` uses it while it waits. Error toasts shake once when they appear, and error and warning toasts are announced with the `alert` accessibility role.

description-and-actions.title: Descriptions & actions
description-and-actions.body: A toast grows a second line when you give it a `description`, and a button when you give it an `action`.
description-and-actions.after: When `successLabel` is set, tapping the button runs `onPress` and then turns the same toast into a success state with that label. Use it for undo flows, where the confirmation should replace the offer instead of stacking a second toast.

promise.title: Promises
promise.body: `toast.promise()` shows a loading toast and morphs it into success or error when the promise settles. Titles and descriptions can be strings or functions of the result.
promise.after:
The loading toast stays until the promise settles; the result then stays for 4 seconds. `toast.promise()` returns the toast handle, not the promise — keep your own reference if you need the result.

`description` and `action` take `success` and `error` keys, and the style options (`fillColor`, `borderColor`, `preset`, `showProgress`…) apply to every phase.

update-and-dismiss.title: Update & dismiss
update-and-dismiss.body: Every call returns a handle with the toast's `id`, an `update()` and a `dismiss()`.
update-and-dismiss.after: `toast.update()` merges new options into a live toast — title, description, variant, action — and the card animates into its new state.
update-and-dismiss.note: Dismissing from code removes the toast at once, without the exit animation. `toast.dismiss()` needs an `id`; called without one it does nothing, so use `toast.dismissAll()` to clear everything.

custom-icons.title: Custom icons
custom-icons.body: Pass any React element as `icon` to replace the variant icon. The variant still decides the title colour and the accessibility role.

headless.title: Reading the toast list
headless.body: `useToasts()` subscribes to the live list, oldest first. Use it to show a count somewhere else in your UI, or to render toasts with a component of your own.
headless.after: Each item is a `Toast`: `{ id, options, dismiss, update }`. Outside React, `toastManager.subscribe(listener)` gives you the same list.

positions.title: Positions
positions.body: Set `position` on the container. `top` and `bottom` centre the stack; the four corners pin it to the edges. Pick one below to move this page's toasts.
positions.after: The stack clears the status bar and home indicator for you: 60 and 40 points on iOS, 40 and 20 on Android. `offset` is added on top of that, and also sets the distance from the side edges for corner positions.
positions.note: `position` on a single toast is in the types but not applied yet — the container decides where toasts go.

theming.title: Theming
theming.body: `theme` takes `light`, `dark` or `system`. With `system` the container follows the device through `useColorScheme()`, and updates when the user switches.
theming.after: The toasts on this page follow the site theme. Switch it in the header to see both.

stacking.title: Stacking
stacking.body: New toasts land on top. Each older toast sits `gap` points further back, scales down 5% and fades 20%. Past `maxVisible`, older toasts fade out completely but stay mounted until they expire.
stacking.after: At most five toasts are kept at once; a sixth pushes out the oldest.

rich-colors.title: Colours & borders
rich-colors.body: `fillColor`, `borderColor` and `borderWidth` restyle one toast's card without touching its layout. Add `showProgress` for a bar that empties over the toast's duration.

animation-presets.title: Motion presets
animation-presets.body: Four presets tune the spring behind the entrance squash and the expand motion. Without one, toasts use a spring with `bounce: 0.4`.
animation-presets.after: For something in between, set `spring` and `bounce` (0 to 1) yourself. `timing.displayDuration` overrides `duration` for auto-dismiss.

style-overrides.title: Style overrides
style-overrides.body: `styles` merges React Native styles over each part of the built-in card. Set it on the container — or app-wide with `<ToastConfigProvider>` — and every toast picks it up.

slots.title: Slots
slots.body: Slots replace one piece of the built-in card and keep the rest: `Icon`, `ActionButton` and `Progress`. Each receives the current `phase` and the resolved accent `color`.
slots.after: A toast's own `icon` option still wins over `slots.Icon`.

custom-layout.title: Custom layout
custom-layout.body: `renderToast` replaces the whole inner card. Blip Toast keeps the parts that are hard to get right — stacking, entrance, error shake, auto-dismiss, promise morphing and accessibility roles — and hands you everything needed to draw the card.
custom-layout.toggle: Use this layout on the page
custom-layout.after: The props are listed under [ToastRenderProps](#api-render-props). Call `dismiss()` for an animated close and `runAction()` to fire the action with its `successLabel` transition.

config-provider.title: App-wide config
config-provider.body: Wrap your app in `<ToastConfigProvider>` to share `styles`, `slots` and `renderToast` with every container below it. Props set directly on a container win, field by field.

api-toast.title: toast()
api-toast.body: The default export. Every method returns a `Toast` handle except `update`, `dismiss` and `dismissAll`.

api-options.title: ToastOptions
api-options.body: The second argument to `toast()` and its variant methods, and what `toast.update()` merges in.

api-container.title: ToastContainer
api-container.body: Mount once. `styles`, `slots` and `renderToast` override `<ToastConfigProvider>` field by field.

api-exports.title: Exports
api-exports.body: Everything the package exports, besides the types above.

methods.error: Show an error toast. It shakes once on entry.
methods.promise: Show a loading toast that becomes success or error when the promise settles.
methods.update: Merge new options into a live toast.
methods.dismiss: Remove the toast with this id. Without an id it does nothing.

options.title: The headline. Set by the first argument of toast().
options.description: Second line under the title. Expands the card.
options.variant: Icon, accent colour and accessibility role.
options.duration: Milliseconds before auto-dismiss. Infinity keeps it until dismissed.
options.action: A button in the card. successLabel turns the toast into a success state after a tap.
options.onDismiss: Called when the toast is removed, for any reason.
options.preset: Spring preset for the entrance and expand motion.
options.spring: Turn the spring on or off, and set its bounce (0–1).
options.showTimestamp: Show the time the toast was created.
options.showProgress: Show a bar that empties over the duration.
options.id: Your own id. Reusing one creates a second toast with the same id.
options.dismissible: Whether the user can dismiss the toast.
options.onPress: Press handler for the whole card.
options.classNames: Class name hooks for web styling.

promise.loading: Title while the promise is pending.
promise.success: Title when it resolves. A function receives the resolved value.
promise.error: Title when it rejects. A function receives the error.
promise.description: Descriptions for the success and error phases. The loading key is in the types but not shown yet.
promise.action: Actions for the success and error phases.
promise.style: Applied to every phase, as in ToastOptions.
promise.onDismiss: Called when the toast is removed.
promise.onAutoClose: Called when the toast closes on its own.

container.theme: Card colour scheme. system follows the device.
container.offset: Extra distance from the screen edges, on top of the safe area.
container.maxVisible: Toasts visible at once; older ones fade into the stack.
container.styles: Style overrides for each part of the built-in card.
container.slots: Replacement components for the icon, action button and progress bar.

render.toast: The toast handle, including its raw options.
render.title: Current title and description.
render.theme: Resolved theme; system is already collapsed.
render.colors: accent, background, surface, text and border, resolved for this toast.
render.timestamp: Localized creation time, such as 3:45 PM.
render.isExpanded: True when there is a description or an action.
render.icon: The default phase icon, or the toast's own.
render.progressBar: A wired progress bar, or null when showProgress is off.
render.dismiss: Animated close, the same path auto-dismiss uses.
render.runAction: Fires action.onPress and runs the successLabel transition.
